ledger.x: c. 2500 BC: the kingdom of Kerma develops at Kerma in Upper Nubia. "developed from around 2500 BC, reaching its peak between 1750 BC and 1500 BC"; the infobox says established c. 2500 BC; Pre-Kerma had developed "between 3500 BC and 2500 BC in Upper Nubia".

c. 1750 BC: Classic Kerma holds the Nile from the First Cataract. The page dates the Classic phase (1750-1500 BC) and the span of control but not the takeover of Lower Nubia from the Egyptian forts (Middle Kingdom, c. 1990-1725 BC): page silent on the year.
1575 BC: Kerma invades deep into Egypt, in partnership with the Hyksos.

1549 BC: Kamose, last Theban king to campaign against Kush, is dated 1554-1549 BC (Ryholt); the page says "Kamose is known to have campaigned against the Kushites prior to his third year" and again in year 4 or 5, and that the Nubians had recaptured Buhen.

c. 1504 BC: Egypt annexes Kerma and Nubia. "the Egyptian annexation of Nubia (Kerma/ Kush) c. 1504 BC"; the Thutmose I page puts his Tombos stele (a fortress "near the third cataract") in his year 2 and says his reign "effectively ended Nubian independence for around 500 years"; Kerma rebellions "continued for 220…
c. 1504 BC: the Kingdom of Kerma ends in the Egyptian annexation; a viceroy of Kush (Turi) is appointed by Thutmose I.

wars.name: Kerma-Hyksos war against Thebes
wars.outcome: Not settled on the pages: the Nubians recaptured Buhen from Kamose, who campaigned against the Kushites before his year 3 and again in year 4 or 5; Egyptian control of Nubia was re-established later.

wars.name: Thutmose I's Nubian campaigns
wars.outcome: Egyptian victory: the Nubian king killed in battle, a fortress built at Tombos, a viceroy of Kush appointed; Nubian independence ended for around 500 years.
